newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Duma head wants no debate on ousting Yeltsin.
newsitem.headline: Duma head wants no debate on ousting Yeltsin.

text.p: The communist chairman of Russia's lower house of parliament said on Thursday the chamber should scratch from its agenda a motion to remove President Boris Yeltsin because of ill health.
His comments further reduced the chances of opposition attempts to oust Yeltsin, who has pneumonia, being successful. The motion has been pencilled in for Friday.

Gennady Seleznyov, speaker of the State Duma lower house, told reporters the chamber should follow the advice of legal experts who said on Wednesday that a vote on the issue would not have legal force.

"I think the issue should be removed (from the agenda) because of the negative assessment from our legal department," said Seleznyov, an influential member of the oposition Communist Party, the biggest faction in the Duma.
The motion was proposed by communist deputy Viktor Ilyukhin, who said Yeltsin's ill health was causing a severe social crisis in Russia.
Communist deputies were due to discuss Ilyukhin's proposal later on Thursday.
Yeltsin has spent almost all the last six months out of the Kremlin, suffering first from heart problems and now from pneumonia.
The chief Kremlin doctor said on Wednesday that the illness was serious and carried the risk of complications, although he added that Yeltsin was recovering and becoming more active.

Doctors say Yeltsin, who was taken to hospital just over a week ago, will stay in hospital for the rest of this week. But they still expect him to be able to attend a summit of leaders of the Commonwealth of Independent States at the end of January.
The Russian constitution is vague on how to remove an ailing head of state, saying only that the president "ceases his functions" if his health is too weak to remain in office.
It does not specify who determines whether the president is too ill or who makes the final decision that he must step down.
